memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, primary open-angle glaucoma, and benign positional vertigo.
Patient reports heartburn after meals, occasional regurgitation, morning eye discomfort with blurred vision, and brief spinning episodes when lying down or turning in bed. On examination, mild epigastric tenderness, normal ocular exteriors with IOP 22 mmHg OD, 21 mmHg OS, and positive Dix-Hallpike on the right side. Smoking status: never smoker. Plan: start pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, antacid gel SOS, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals; timolol 0.5% eye drops BD; latanoprost 0.005% eye drops HS; betahistine 16 mg BD; meclizine 25 mg SOS for vertigo SOS.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: H. pylori stool antigen: negative (reference: negative).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dix-Hallpike test: positive on right side with torsional nystagmus lasting <1 minute, consistent with benign positional vertigo right posterior canal.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Stable GERD, glaucoma, and improving BPV.
Patient reports reduced heartburn frequency, occasional eye strain, and only one brief vertigo episode in past two weeks after performing Epley maneuver at home. Examination: mild epigastric tenderness, IOP 21 mmHg OD, 20 mmHg OS, Dix-Hallpike now negative. Smoking status: never smoker. Plan: continue current meds; consider tapering domperidone if asymptomatic; reinforce vertigo exercises.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: GERD controlled, glaucoma stable, BPV resolved.
Patient denies heartburn for past month, uses antacid gel only occasionally. Reports no vertigo episodes since last visit; Epley maneuver performed successfully. Eye comfort unchanged; IOP stable. Smoking status: never smoker. Plan: discontinue domperidone; continue pantoprazole and glaucoma drops; continue betahistine as prophylaxis; meclizine PRN only.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: GERD on maintenance therapy, glaucoma well-controlled, no vertigo recurrence.
Patient reports occasional mild heartburn after spicy food, relieved by antacid gel. No eye pain or vision change. No vertigo episodes. Examination: IOP 20 mmHg OD, 19 mmHg OS; visual fields full; optic discs normal. Smoking status: never smoker. Plan: continue current meds; schedule IOP check in 3 months; consider annual visual field test.
